name: pump_scheduling
description: Two-pump water plant scheduling against a time-of-use tariff, framed as a flexibility-versus-storage trade-off. A feed pump fills a tank across a fixed pressure differential; a product pump draws from the tank to meet a fixed user demand profile. The comparison is a 2x2: an inflexible facility (feed pump held at a constant duty for all 24 hours) or a flexible one (feed pump scheduled against the tariff), each paired with a large or a small battery.

fluid._comment: The raw-water source is a flex-pse Feed block; suction_pressure_bar is its boundary condition. Density is a property-package constant.

feed_pump._comment: Pumps into the tank. In the flexible strategy it is semicontinuous: either off, or anywhere in [min_flow_fraction, 1.0] of rated flow. In the inflexible strategy it is pinned at a single constant flow for the whole horizon (see model.inflexible_flow_m3_per_hr). delta_pressure_bar is the fixed pressure differential across the pump. start_stop_cost is a degradation penalty in $ per on/off transition, so the flexible schedule pays for every start and stop it makes.

tank._comment: Sized so the flexible strategy can pre-fill and ride the whole peak window on stored water, but so the inflexible strategy -- which cannot pre-fill, because its pump never modulates -- gains nothing from it. The tank is cyclic: it has to end the day at least as full as it started (Tank(cyclic=True)).

product_pump._comment: Draws from the tank and delivers to the customer, a flex-pse Product block whose per-hour min_demand is product_demand_m3_per_hr. It is an inflexible load under either strategy.

battery._comment: Sizing options are fractions of the plant's peak electrical load (see reference_load_kw): power ratings are fraction * peak load, and energy capacity is fraction * peak load * storage_duration_hours. The battery is cyclic: it ends the day at least as charged as it started. wear_cost_per_kwh is a throughput degradation penalty on every kWh discharged. The capital_* fields annualize the battery's installed cost with flexops.costing.capital_recovery_factor; that is reported beside the operating cost, not optimized.

scenarios._comment: The 2x2. 'flexible' selects the feed pump strategy; 'battery' names a key of battery.sizing_options. 'selected' is the case the single-schedule charts render.
